biggest_catch: HVAC measures require a licensed or affiliated program installer — you can't DIY the big-ticket rebates, and the installer must meet Georgia Power's requirements.
catches: Air-source heat pump conversion, HPWH, mini-split, and ground-source measures require a licensed professional or affiliated program installer.
Heat-pump water heater rebate (up to $800) is an instant rebate applied through the affiliated installer.
Application within 60 days of the paid-in-full invoice/receipt.
Georgia Power residential customer with meter number.
The equipment purchase/installation is a condition, not an upfront fee.

c2.evidence: Official HEIP services table: conversion to air-source heat pump up to $1,500; heat-pump water heater up to $800 (instant via installer); ductless mini-split $500; ground-source $300.

c3.evidence: No enrollment fee; equipment purchase/installation is a purchase condition.

eligibility: Georgia Power residential customer. Licensed professional or affiliated program installer required for HVAC/heat-pump measures. Application within 60 days of paid-in-full invoice. Meter number required.
notes: Verified on the official Georgia Power HEIP page 2026-09-22. The HPWH rebate is instant through the installer; other heat-pump rebates are mail-in style.

steps: Use Georgia Power's installer finder to pick an affiliated program installer (or licensed professional for HVAC).
Have the heat-pump conversion or water-heater work completed; the HPWH rebate is applied instantly through the installer.
Keep your paid-in-full invoice and meter number.
Submit the HEIP rebate application within 60 days of the invoice date for non-instant measures.
Receive your rebate check after the typical 6–8 week processing window.
timing: Rebate processing typically takes 6–8 weeks for a complete application; heat-pump water heater rebate is instant through the affiliated installer.
